The Overlord has received our requests for parley, and our informants indicate that he may be willing to spare the remaining sacrifices from your village.”}}<div class="wv-epigraph-cite">{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|— ''House of Blades'', chapter 16}}</div></div>
''See also: [[Overlord (The Traveler's Gate Trilogy) Timeline]]''

== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|Overlords are high-ranking figures tasked with the vital responsibility of ensuring that [[Incarnations]] remain imprisoned. Because they command heavily defended territories, attacking an Overlord is generally considered a dangerous undertaking. These leaders serve various thrones and can be associated with different realms; for instance, one Overlord served the [[throne]] of [[Damasca]], while another was a [[Traveler]] from [[Naraka]], a territory characterized by law and moral order. The role of an Overlord can vary significantly depending on their origin, such as [[Deborah]], an Overlord associated with [[Ornheim]], who utilized the disciplined nature of her territory's [[Travelers]]. While some Overlords like [[Malachi]] have been identified as [[Travelers]] of specific territories, the position itself is a distinct office of [[Authority|authority]] and duty.}}

== Personality ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|The Overlord is a powerful figure who holds prisoners of war and serves the [[throne]] of [[Damasca]]. This being maintains an alliance with his [[Travelers]] and the [[Grandmasters]].}}

== Relationships ==
{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|[[Leah]] is a person who was personally taken by the Overlord and intends to speak with him. The Overlord maintains an alliance with his [[Travelers]] and the [[Grandmasters]].}}

== History ==
=== {{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|The House of Blades}} ===
{{spoiler|book=tg-01-house-of-blades|[[Leah]] intends to speak with the Overlord regarding certain matters, a figure who holds prisoners of war.<ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c2">''House of Blades'', chapter 2</ref><ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c4">''House of Blades'', chapter 4</ref> This power is something the local villagers cannot stand up to, and children recognize Overlords as a class of powerful beings.<ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c5">''House of Blades'', chapter 5</ref><ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c11">''House of Blades'', chapter 11</ref> While the Overlord has received requests for parley and maintains a Master of Household, they are also the figure whom the [[Myrians]] are standing against.<ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c16">''House of Blades'', chapter 16</ref><ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c17">''House of Blades'', chapter 17</ref> After the Overlord personally took [[Leah]], [[Simon]] eventually killed an Overlord.<ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c17" /><ref name="tg-01-house-of-blades-c22">''House of Blades'', chapter 22</ref>}}

=== {{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|Post-Overlord Era}} ===
{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|The Overlord is deceased.<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c2">''The Crimson Vault'', chapter 2</ref> Historically, each individual holding this title was responsible for guarding a single [[Hanging Tree]].<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c9">''The Crimson Vault'', chapter 9</ref> The Overlord maintained an alliance consisting of his [[Travelers]] and the [[Grandmasters]].<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c16">''The Crimson Vault'', chapter 16</ref> This position served as a title for those who acted in service to the [[throne]] of [[Damasca]].<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c18">''The Crimson Vault'', chapter 18</ref>}}

<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|The Overlord is in an alliance with the [[Grandmasters]] and his [[Travelers]].<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c16" />}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=tg-02-crimson-vault|An Overlord is a title for someone serving the [[throne]] of [[Damasca]].<ref name="tg-02-crimson-vault-c18" />}}</li>
